annotation.title_clean: Regulation (EU) 2017/746 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 April 2017 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices and repealing Directive 98/79/EC and Commission Decision 2010/227/EU
annotation.title_en: Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union L 117
annotation.summary_en: EU Regulation 2017/746 sets rules for placing in vitro diagnostic medical devices on the EU market. It establishes four risk classes, notified-body conformity assessment, performance evaluation and studies, UDI traceability, the Eudamed database, vigilance and market surveillance, and manufacturer liability coverage, replacing Directive 98/79/EC. It has no AI or robotics provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Four risk classes (A-D) with notified-body involvement for classes B-D
Manufacturers must run risk management, quality management and post-market surveillance systems
CE marking, harmonised standards and common specifications give presumption of conformity
UDI system and Eudamed database for traceability and transparency
Financial coverage for liability and authorised representative joint liability
